extracted.intended_audience: senior biomedical researchers considering applying to the HHMI Investigator Program
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for scientists applying to the Howard Hughes Medical Institute (HHMI) Investigator Program, including eligibility, application materials, and the attributes HHMI seeks in investigators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify and pursue significant biological questions
rubrics_metrics.description: They identify and pursue significant biological questions in a rigorous and deep manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHMI looks for investigators who focus on important biological problems and approach them with rigor and depth. This attribute is explicitly used in review of applicants and renewals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ask tough questions even at risk of failure
rubrics_metrics.description: They ask tough questions in science, even at the risk of failure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHMI supports people rather than projects and values investigators willing to tackle high-risk, high-reward fundamental questions. This is emphasized as a cultural expectation of HHMI investigators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drive field into new areas of inquiry
rubrics_metrics.description: They drive their chosen research field into new areas of inquiry, being consistently at its forefront.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should demonstrate leadership that pushes their field forward and establishes new directions of inquiry rather than incremental work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop new tools and methods / interdisciplinary approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: They develop new tools and methods that enable creative experimental approaches to biological questions, bringing to bear concepts or techniques from other disciplines when necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHMI values methodological and technical innovation, including interdisciplinary approaches that create capabilities to address previously intractable problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forge links between basic biology and medicine
rubrics_metrics.description: They forge links between basic biology and medicine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigators who connect fundamental biological discovery to medical understanding or applications are favorably viewed; translation-oriented connections are part of the desired profile.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promise of future original and innovative contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: They demonstrate great promise of future original and innovative contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection considers not only past achievements but evidence that the applicant will continue producing original, innovative work in the future.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active in service and training / mentorship
rubrics_metrics.description: They are active in service and training in their host institutions, and in the greater scientific community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHMI expects investigators to contribute to mentoring, training, and service activities locally and within the broader community; such contributions are evaluated during selection and renewals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Degree requirement (PhD and/or MD)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must hold a PhD and/or MD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a basic eligibility requirement; specific competitions may state additional degree-related details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible institutional affiliation (U.S. institutions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must plan to perform research at one of over 200 eligible U.S. institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants need to be based at an institution on HHMI's eligible-institutions list; the program is tied to performing research at an eligible U.S. host.

rubrics_metrics.name: Position representing substantial institutional commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must hold a position that represents substantial commitment by their institution, such as a tenure-track faculty position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The applicant's host institution must demonstrate substantial commitment to the candidate (e.g., tenure-track or equivalent), since appointments involve collaborative agreements with host institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track record of peer-reviewed funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must have a track record of peer-reviewed funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior success in obtaining peer-reviewed grants or fellowships is an eligibility/selection factor demonstrating independence and capacity to lead a research program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum post-training professional experience (competition-specific)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each competition defines a required length of post-training professional experience prior to the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must meet the experience window specified in the particular competition announcement (varies by competition).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of scientific disciplines (competition-specific)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each competition defines the breadth of scientific disciplines to be considered; however, most competitions are open to all biomedical disciplines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should check the specific competition announcement to confirm whether their discipline is eligible; by default, most HHMI Investigator competitions accept applications across biomedical fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required application materials (CV, five highlighted articles, program description)
rubrics_metrics.description: Application requirements include a CV, five highlighted research articles, and a program description focused on research achievements during the last five years and future research plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program description should emphasize recent accomplishments (last five years) and articulate future research directions. The five highlighted articles are selected to represent the applicant's most significant contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct application process / no nomination / no institutional limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants apply directly; there is no nomination process and no limit of the number of applications from a single institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The open application model means candidates self-nominate and institutions may submit multiple applicants without internal selection constraints imposed by HHMI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection by HHMI leadership based on external assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection of investigators is made by HHMI scientific leadership and is based on assessment by a panel of distinguished scientists, including members of HHMI advisory boards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation is peer-based: panels of distinguished scientists assess applicants and HHMI leadership makes appointment decisions informed by these assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seven-year renewable appointment and renewal assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: The HHMI investigator appointment has a seven-year renewable term. Renewal decisions are made by HHMI scientific leadership, based on assessment by a panel of distinguished scientists, including members of HHMI advisory boards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Renewal is not automatic; investigators are re-evaluated by the same peer-review/leadership process and must demonstrate continued excellence and alignment with HHMI investigator attributes.
